phase: M4 — first three read-only MCP capabilities
scope: list_properties, get_property, get_tenant. Module only — no transport is mounted. No search_property_memory, CAM/attention/timeline/evidence/dispute/payment tools, no Ripple, no write tools, no approval workflows, no UI, no Pilot, no Production, no CAM repair.

transport_note.what_was_built: a capability module exporting MCP-shaped tool descriptors (name, description, inputSchema, handler) plus a call(name,args,ctx) dispatcher
transport_note.what_was_not: no HTTP route, no MCP server process, no socket. Mounting a transport exposes an external surface, and the brief said build only the three capabilities.
transport_note.to_mount_later: a transport needs only to pass the caller Authorization header through as ctx.token and return the envelope verbatim

headline_finding.what: A property row whose data blob was never written answered "no disputes" instead of "nothing has been recorded".
headline_finding.detail: The hydrator reads d.disputes || [] from row.data || {}. A property created but never saved therefore produced empty spaces, disputes, timeline and documents — indistinguishable from a property that genuinely has none. An MCP client asking "does this property have any disputes?" would have been told no.
headline_finding.fix: The hydrator now reports degraded["property.no_stored_record"] when row.data is absent, and the capability layer maps that to section status UNAVAILABLE, returning null rather than []. meta.unavailable is untouched, because assemble() DID compose every section — from nothing.
headline_finding.why_it_matters_here: This is the first phase where the semantics leave the building. A caveat in a sibling field does not stop a client reading data.disputes.length === 0; null does.

four_states.empty: composed, source present, genuinely none — returned as []
four_states.degraded: composed from fewer inputs — returned with the rows and a caveat
four_states.unavailable: could not be composed, or nothing was ever recorded — returned as null
four_states.ordering: unavailable outranks degraded outranks empty, asserted directly as a contract (G9a-G9k)
four_states.unknown_vs_less: tenants.read_failed and property.no_stored_record mean UNKNOWN and force null; tenants.from_table_no_review_state and attention.without_selectors_readiness mean KNOWN-FROM-LESS and keep their rows

security.identity: handlers take a token and resolve the user server-side. There is deliberately no userId parameter.
security.only_id_crosses: resolveIdentity returns {ok,userId} and nothing else. Not role, not app_metadata, not user_metadata — the last is user-writable in Supabase.
security.ownership: properties.user_id = authenticated user. Nothing else confers it.
security.second_identity_space: tenant_users (migration 012) links an auth user to a tenant space and carries a property_id. A tenant-portal user therefore holds a valid session for a property they do not own. They get an empty portfolio and a refusal — tested in section D.
fail_closed: blank token refuses without contacting the auth service
an auth payload with no id refuses
an auth timeout refuses, and is distinguished from a bad token
a failed list read returns null, not an empty portfolio

reads.list_properties: ONE read: /properties?user_id=eq.<uid>&select=id,name,sqft,created_at,updated_at,archived_at — the blob is deliberately not selected and no property is hydrated
reads.get_property: the three approved M1b reads via the accepted hydrator
reads.get_tenant: the same three; the tenant is found with find() inside the owned record, never fetched by id

gaps_the_first_run_exposed: I-userid-from-args-getprop and I-list-uses-arg-userid — the most serious of the set. A caller-supplied userId was honoured, and every existing refusal happened BEFORE the argument was reachable, so none of them proved it was ignored. Now tested with a VALID tenant session naming the owner (B7a-B7g).
S-null-value-not-unavailable — a null section could be reclassified empty; the ordering rules are now asserted as a contract, not only through fixtures (G9a-G9k).
X-documents-not-scoped — the fixture only gave documents to one tenant, so filtered and unfiltered produced the same list. Both tenants now have documents (F18a-F18d).

mutation_m1b.survivor: D-prune-removed — the same equivalent mutant reported since M1b, unchanged
